Team —

Quick summary and ask: NovaCare (Series B clinical triage vendor) is asking for a deep discount on Hosted API usage to match a competing vendor. They are proposing a 24–36 month commitment with an expected spend ramp to roughly $1.2M ARR by year 2 (see attached forecast). They want a blended unit rate that is ~30% below our standard hosted list.

Why this is strategic:
- They plan to list us in their marketplace and co-market to five hospital systems in Q1 of next year.
- Strong reference potential in a key health vertical where our visibility is low.
- They have procurement bandwidth for a single PO and prefer an annual prepayment option.

Proposed commercial structure I negotiated with the customer:
- Year 1: 30% off hosted usage list if they prepay 12 months up front.
- Year 2: 25% off with minimum committed volume; price floors apply.
- 12-month minimum term; auto-renew unless notice.
- Redwood to provide a marketing credit ($25k) tied to joint webinars.

Ask: I need executive sign-off for the >20% concession and any additional conditions (prepay, caps on credits, SLA credit exposure). Ben — can you confirm recommended guardrails and whether finance/legal require anything additional? Laura/Rishi — need your read on how to structure the revenue recognition / prepay condition. Marissa — would appreciate a final commercial signoff or escalation guidance.

I think this is a net-positive strategic play, but I don’t want to proceed without formal approval for the >20% off request.

Karthik — thanks for the concise write-up and attachments. I looked through the forecast and competitive context. My read: the ask is reasonable for a strategic pilot that can convert into a larger account, but we should lock several guardrails before approving the 30% level.

Recommended deal guardrails (Deal Desk):
- Approve up to 30% off list in Year 1 only with the following conditions:
  - Customer prepays 12 months (non-refundable cap tied to committed volume).
  - Minimum committed spend of $600k in Year 1 (to avoid loss-leading small deals).
  - Limit marketing credit to $25k and apply as service credit, not against recurring usage.
  - Cap SLA credits exposure at 1% of annual contract value.
- Year 2 pricing re-evaluated after usage pattern; do not auto-extend 30% unless metrics are met.
- Add a kill-switch clause: if monthly usage falls below 40% of forecast for consecutive 3 months, revert to standard list or terminate.

Please confirm the prepay language with Finance and Legal. If everyone agrees, this is the package I recommend we present to the customer. I also suggest we require a signature on the redline terms (attached) and an explicit PO referencing the deal id.

-Ben
